page: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and 4th Generation Intel Xeon Scalable processors (model 8488C). Utilizing x86_64 architecture, this instance supplies 32 vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled at a 3.2 GHz base clock. The processor features 105 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and hardware acceleration via Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets. It is provisioned with 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory clocked at 5 GHz, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio at 2.0 GB per vCPU. No local NVMe storage is bundled with the instance, requiring network-attached storage solutions, while network throughput provides a baseline bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong single-thread efficiency and cryptographic execution. Geekbench testing yields a single-core score of 2074.0 and a multi-core score of 15951.0, both placing in the upper quartile. Passmark encryption operations score 35678.6, reflecting dedicated hardware cryptographic acceleration (AES, VAES, SHA-NI). Throughput workloads demonstrate high performance in web delivery, with static web serving reaching 51.12 GB/sec. Data processing tests show rapid single-threaded decompression and compression rates, achieving 33.6 GB/sec in gzip compression and 13.85 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression, alongside small-model LLM text generation rates of 286.26 tokens per second.

The c7i-flex instance family operates on a burstable CPU allocation model designed for workloads that do not continuously utilize full CPU capacity. This architecture offers a cost-effective alternative to fixed compute configurations by providing high peak processing density without the expense of dedicated baseline execution. However, workloads requiring persistent full-throttle compute may encounter resource constraints due to the burstable vCPU design, and the absence of bundled local storage requires budgeting for independent network volume capacity. The hardware configuration makes this server type well aligned for high-traffic web applications, continuous integration pipelines, batch text processing, and microservice container clusters.
